newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Renault workers to demonstrate in France.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Renault workers to demonstrate in France.

text.p: Workers from French carmaker Renault's doomed plant at Vilvoorde in Belgium will stage a protest demonstration in northern France on Thursday, the Belga news agency reported.

The morning shift of the plant, which only returned to work last week after a six-week strike following Renault's shock announcement on February 27 that it would close Vilvoorde in July, will head to Lille in the hope of meeting French Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin.
"We will ask him to keep the plant open if his party wins the elections," one union source told Belga on Tuesday.
President Jacques Chirac said on Monday France would hold two-part general elections on May 25 and June 1.

A court in Belgium and another in France have ruled that Renault failed to follow worker consultation procedures when it announced the closure of the profitable Vilvoorde plant, and must therefore restart the procedures from scratch.
The closure decision shocked Belgians, chilled the diplomatic atmosphere between the two countries and triggered a series of demonstrations in Belgium and France.
Renault is appealing against the rulings, and Chairman Louis Schweitzer has repeatedly said that while the closure of the plant may be slightly delayed it will not be revoked.
